title: Rotterdam Port Workers Strike Over Welfare Cuts Meant to Fund Higher NATO Defense Spending
detail: The FNV Havens trade union struck at the ports of Rotterdam, Amsterdam and Zeeland from 11:15 to 19:00 on September 4, 2026 — one of nine days of Dutch labor action in September against the government's plan to cut up to €6.5 billion in annual welfare spending, mainly by shortening the maximum unemployment-benefit period from two years to one, to help finance the Netherlands' higher NATO defense-spending commitments. Bloomberg framed the walkout explicitly as workers striking 'to fund higher NATO spend.' Thousands of railway operators, bus drivers, metalworkers, Heineken employees and civil servants joined the broader mobilization, one of the largest in the Netherlands in recent years. The centre-right minority government, which lacks a parliamentary majority, had already offered concessions — dropping a plan to accelerate the state pension age increase — but the left-wing opposition Pro party said the changes were insufficient and sided with the unions in demanding the welfare cuts be withdrawn entirely.

media.caption: Dutch port and transport workers strike over welfare cuts intended to fund higher NATO defense spending
